meta.title: E-commerce Checkout
meta.summary: Place an order, reserve stock and charge the card exactly once, with a saga to undo work when payment fails.

functional: Place an order from a cart
nonFunctional: Never sell more units than are in stock
Survive payment provider timeouts and outages

nodes.label: Payment Service
nodes.description: Wraps the payment provider; owns idempotency and reconciliation

nodes.label: Orders DB
nodes.description: orders + outbox tables in one database

nodes.label: Outbox Relay
nodes.description: Publishes committed outbox rows to the event stream

flows.title: Place order
flows.summary: Idempotent order creation, atomic stock reservation, an idempotent charge, and a transactional outbox for the follow-up events.

steps.label: POST /orders
steps.detail: The client creates an idempotency key once per checkout attempt and reuses it on retries.

steps.label: auth + rate limit
steps.detail: During flash sales the gateway can also hold excess users in a virtual waiting room.

steps.label: INSERT order PENDING
steps.detail: A unique constraint on the idempotency key: a retry gets the existing order back instead of creating a second one.

steps.label: conditional UPDATE
steps.detail: One atomic statement: it only succeeds while stock remains, so two buyers can never both get the last pair. No distributed lock needed.

steps.label: 1 row updated
steps.detail: Zero rows would mean sold out. Reservations expire after 15 minutes if the order never completes.

steps.label: charge, key = o_501
steps.detail: If the provider times out, retry with the same key. The provider returns the original result rather than charging twice.

steps.label: UPDATE PAID + INSERT outbox
steps.detail: Transactional outbox: the status change and the OrderPaid event commit together. There is never a paid order without its event, or an event without the order.

steps.label: poll outbox
steps.detail: Or tail the database change log (CDC). Either way, only committed rows are published.

steps.label: publish OrderPaid
steps.detail: At-least-once: consumers deduplicate by event id.

flows.title: Payment declined (saga rollback)
flows.summary: No distributed transaction: each completed step has a compensating action that undoes it.

steps.label: release reservation
steps.detail: Compensating action for the reservation. It is idempotent too, so a retried release cannot add stock twice.

steps.label: UPDATE available + 1
steps.payload:
UPDATE stock SET available = available + 1, reserved = reserved - 1
WHERE sku = 'SHOE-42';  -- guarded by reservation id

steps.label: UPDATE FAILED + outbox
steps.detail: OrderFailed is published the same way as OrderPaid.

steps.label: Card declined, try another
steps.detail: The same cart can be retried with a new idempotency key.

notes.text: Saga instead of a distributed transaction: services stay independent and available; the cost is writing a compensating action for every step and accepting brief intermediate states.
Transactional outbox fixes the dual-write problem: writing to the database and publishing an event separately can fail halfway; one transaction cannot.
On a timeout the charge state is unknown. Retry with the same idempotency key; if still unknown, leave the order PENDING and let a reconciliation job query the provider.
A single hot SKU in a flash sale concentrates writes on one row. Split its stock into several buckets (rows) and reserve from any bucket with stock.
Kafka replicates each partition across 3 zones; with one zone down it still has a majority of replicas and keeps accepting writes.
